title: Strict tower homotopy limit
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, whose objects are strict inverse sequences and whose exactness is levelwise. On its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], total right derived inverse limit is computed by taking a K-injective tower resolution and then termwise inverse limit [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. This gives an exact functor $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to D(\mathcal A)$. For every strict tower complex $X_\bullet$ there is a natural distinguished triangle $R\lim X_\bullet\to\prod_n^D X_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n^D X_n\to(R\lim X_\bullet)[1]$ [def-weil-derived-limit], where $\prod^D$ is the product in $D(\mathcal A)$ and the $n$-th component of $s$ is transition followed by projection to $n+1$. In particular, if for every $n$ some transition $X_m\to X_n$, $m\geq n$, is zero in $D(\mathcal A)$, then $R\lim X_\bullet=0$. If $v:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$ is a strict map of tower complexes whose tower of mapping cones has that property, then the canonical map $R\lim(v)$ is an isomorphism. No exactness of countable products in $\mathcal A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), in particular Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); the proof works for modules using the constant pullback ring sheaf on the tower site. Pro-zero consequence: the finite geometric-series inverse of 1-s, or Tag 0H9L (more-algebra-lemma-pro-isomorphism-Rlim) in more-algebra.tex, applied to the zero tower. Strict functoriality uses the total derived functor on the tower site.

proof.text: For a small site, apply the existing source Grothendieck theorem for module sheaves directly. For independent coefficient universes, first transport module sheaves to the coefficient-universe small site and use equivalence invariance. In the tower category, the coproduct of the evaluation-left-adjoint images of a separator is a separator; filtered colimits and exactness are levelwise. Apply the existing Grothendieck K-injective-resolution construction to obtain functorial tower resolutions with injective terms.

Apply the source rightDerivedFunctor construction to the additive inverse-limit functor. Whisker its homotopy-category unit with the quotient and the quotientCompQhIso comparisons. The K-injective derivability structure proves that this is a total right derived functor on complexes, since its unit is invertible on K-injectives. The source triangulated instance gives its shift and triangulated structures.

Use products of K-injectives to obtain countable products in the derived category. Exact tower evaluation inverts quasi-isomorphisms levelwise, so localization supplies E and its comparison ε. For a degreewise injective tower resolution, extend the identity map from the evaluation left-adjoint prefix tower across its monic inclusion in the next prefix tower: this splits each transition. Recursively solving y_n - q_n y_(n+1) = x_n gives a section of 1-s in every degree. The limit cone is its kernel by the product universal property and compatibility of all tower maps. Thus 0 → lim I → product I → product I → 0 is a short exact sequence of complexes. Evaluation preserves K-injectives; the termwise-product theorem identifies its localized products with the chosen derived products. The short-exact-sequence triangle is distinguished.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), proof: injective transitions, exact left adjoint to evaluation, and the short exact product sequence; derived.tex Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective).

proof.text: Form natural transformations lim → product and 1-s on tower complexes, and apply them to the functorial K-injective resolution with injective terms. Naturality of the short-exact-sequence connecting morphism gives a natural connecting map. The unit η and localization of the resolution quasi-isomorphism give a natural isomorphism from localized resolved limits to Q ⋙ RF. The product comparison, localization of the resolution map and ε give a natural isomorphism from localized resolved products to Q ⋙ E ⋙ product. The latter intertwines 1-s, by naturality of the tower transition endomorphism and the projection formula for the product comparison. Transport the short-exact-sequence triangle along these isomorphisms. Full faithfulness of precomposition with the localization Q descends the first and connecting natural transformations to the derived tower category. Essential surjectivity of Q transports distinguishedness to all derived objects.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits) and Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); natural short-exact-sequence triangle, derived.tex Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor).

proof.text: Suppose the evaluated tower is pro-zero in $D(\mathcal A)$. Write $P=\prod_n^D X_n$ and $s:P\to P$ for its shift endomorphism. For each $n$ choose $r_n\geq1$ such that $\mathrm{pr}_n s^{r_n}=0$: a zero transition $X_m\to X_n$ gives $r_n=m-n$ when $m>n$, and if $m=n$ then $X_n=0$ and take $r_n=1$. Define $t:P\to P$ by $\mathrm{pr}_n t=\sum_{k=0}^{r_n-1}\mathrm{pr}_n s^k$, using the product universal property [def-weil-category-product]. All later summands vanish, so these finite sums are unchanged upon increasing $r_n$. Telescoping gives $\mathrm{pr}_n t(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n$. Also $f_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}t=\sum_{k=1}^{r_{n+1}}\mathrm{pr}_n s^k=\sum_{k\geq1}\mathrm{pr}_n s^k$ (a finite sum), since $\mathrm{pr}_n s^{r_{n+1}+1}=f_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}s^{r_{n+1}}=0$. Hence $\mathrm{pr}_n(1-s)t=\mathrm{pr}_n$, and $t$ is a two-sided inverse of $1-s$. In the Roos triangle $H\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow{\delta}H[1]$, consecutive composites are zero [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], so $p=0$ and $\delta=0$ because $1-s$ is invertible. Rotate the triangle backwards [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $P[-1]\xrightarrow{-\delta[-1]}H\xrightarrow{p}P\to P$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(H,-)$ at $H$ [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] factors $\mathrm{id}_H$ through $-\delta[-1]=0$. Thus $\mathrm{id}_H=0$ and $H=R\lim X_\bullet$ is a zero object. This is a coordinatewise finite calculation, requiring no uniform nilpotence bound or exactness of products.

source.place: Tag 0H9L (lemma-pro-isomorphism-Rlim), pro-zero case; explicit finite-series calculation in the Roos triangle of derived.tex Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit).

proof.text: For a strict chain map $v:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$, its mapping cone $C(v)$ is formed in the tower category; evaluation gives $C(v)_n=C(v_n)$ by the degreewise biproduct-and-differential formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The cone triangle $X_\bullet\xrightarrow{v}Y_\bullet\to C(v)\to X_\bullet[1]$ is distinguished. Exactness of $R\lim$ from the total derived construction, supplied by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], gives a distinguished triangle whose first arrow is the canonical $u=R\lim(v)$. Under the hypothesis on the cone tower, the pro-zero calculation makes its third vertex zero. Put $A=R\lim X_\bullet$ and $B=R\lim Y_\bullet$. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(B,-)$ in $A\xrightarrow{u}B\to0\to A[1]$ [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $r:B\to A$ with $ur=\mathrm{id}_B$. Apply the same exactness statement to the backwards rotated triangle $0[-1]\to A\xrightarrow{u}B\to0$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]: $u(ru-\mathrm{id}_A)=0$ implies that $ru-\mathrm{id}_A$ factors through $0[-1]$, so it is zero. Therefore $r$ is a two-sided inverse and the canonical $R\lim(v)$ is an isomorphism.
